analysis: What changed vs Monday's 9:00 AM brief: the drift lower became a rout. Monday closed with the S&P 500 -1.92% at 7,416.59 and the Nasdaq -2.49%, a third straight down day, and futures are still pointing lower this morning (S&P -0.4% at ~6:44 AM ET) rather than bouncing. The new structural piece is the Commerce Department's interim chip-export rule, which turns the Nvidia story from a governance/earnings event into a demand story: licenses now gate advanced chips to five countries and cloud compute above ~750 H100/H200s to restricted firms, effective Nov 19, and Nvidia is reportedly already tightening supply conditions for customers leasing heavily to Chinese firms (Reuters has not verified that part). Tonight's print is therefore judged less on the quarter itself, which ended Oct 25 before Huang resigned, and more on guidance and what Kress says about forward demand, with the HN scarcity thread adding a credibility question about how much AI demand was Nvidia-financed. The counterweight is Anthropic: a ~7x oversubscribed book closing today shows primary-market AI appetite is intact even as public AI stocks de-risk, though those orders are non-binding and funds routinely over-order expecting cuts. Macro stays restrictive: a December hike is now fully priced (100% per FedWatch) and Warsh's Monday scenarios included weaker investment returns and falling valuations. Signal vs noise: the price action (VIX 22.91, 10Y 5.15%, Nasdaq in correction territory, only staples green) is the signal; the Huang comeback lobbying and petition are noise until the board or a filing moves. Everything funnels into tonight: Nvidia after the close and October retail sales at 8:30 AM ET.

headlines.headline: Futures point lower after Monday's rout: S&P 500 futures -0.4%, Dow -0.5%, Nasdaq 100 -0.5% as of ~6:44 AM ET. Monday closed with the S&P 500 -1.92% at 7,416.59, the Nasdaq -2.49% at 24,509.76 and the Dow -1.41% at 51,608.17 (-739 points). SPY was -0.44% premarket at $736.66; QQQ -0.45%, DIA -0.50%.
headlines.why_it_matters: No bounce after three straight down days — sellers are still in control into the open, with the tape waiting on tonight's Nvidia print.

headlines.headline: Nvidia slips ~1% further premarket into tonight's earnings, its first report since Jensen Huang resigned Nov 12. Results land ~4:20 PM ET with the call at 5:00 PM ET, interim CEO Colette Kress's first. Consensus is ~$109B revenue (vs the company's $108B guidance, +/-2%) and ~$2.47-2.49 EPS; options price an ~8.5% move. Shares closed Monday at $156.14 (-4.12%), their lowest since July 2025 and below the $204.02 200-day average since Nov 4.
headlines.why_it_matters: The stock keeps leaking into the print, so the bar is guidance and demand commentary, not the quarter itself — the quarter ended Oct 25, before Huang left.

headlines.headline: Commerce's interim chip-export rule lands: the Bureau of Industry and Security now requires licences to ship advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and licences for overseas data centers supplying more than ~12M total processing performance (roughly 750 H100/H200 chips) of compute to firms in China or other restricted countries. Existing operators have 90 days to comply; the rule takes effect Nov 19 and rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 5.28% Monday.
headlines.why_it_matters: This turns the Nvidia story from a one-stock governance event into a structural demand overhang for the whole chip complex — the rule targets remote compute access, not just physical exports.

headlines.headline: Nvidia is reportedly tightening supply conditions for some data-center customers: it warned customers that pending US legislation on remote computing access could expose the company and operators to legal action, and will not keep selling chips to customers leasing more than 50% of their GPU capacity to Chinese enterprises. Reuters has not independently verified the report and Nvidia did not comment.
headlines.why_it_matters: If true, Nvidia is pre-emptively cutting off a demand channel before the rules bite — single-source, unconfirmed, treat as fragile until Nvidia or a filing confirms it.

headlines.headline: Home Depot Q3: sales $43.4B (+4.9%), adjusted EPS $3.86 (about in line with the ~$3.84-3.86 consensus), comparable sales +2.2%, and updated fiscal 2026 guidance of ~4.5% sales growth. Shares were -1.59% premarket at $342 (vs Monday's $347.51 close). Earnings call at 9:00 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: A roughly in-line print that the market is shrugging at — the consumer read matters more than the stock move, with October retail sales due at 8:30 AM ET.

headlines.headline: Disney reports fiscal Q4 before the open (call 8:30 AM ET): consensus ~$1.67-1.68 EPS on ~$25.2-25.4B revenue. Shares were +1.81% premarket at $120.85 (vs Monday's $118.70 close).
headlines.why_it_matters: One of the few premarket gainers — the print and fiscal 2027 guidance will set the tone for media and consumer discretionary into the open.

headlines.headline: Anthropic's IPO book is ~7x oversubscribed (Bloomberg), with the order book closing today. Bankers are weighing pricing above the $70-78 range when the deal prices Wednesday; first trade is Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. The 825M-share offering would raise ~$64.4B at the top of the range (~$1.4T fully diluted). Seven strategic partners, including Google and Nvidia at ~$10B each, have agreed to buy $26B of stock at the IPO price.
headlines.why_it_matters: Primary-market AI appetite looks intact even as public AI stocks sell off — but orders are non-binding and funds routinely over-order expecting cuts, so the multiple measures appetite, not money committed.

headlines.headline: A December Fed hike is now fully priced: CME FedWatch shows markets assigning a 100% probability to a rate increase after the December meeting, up from ~92% on Monday. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh on Monday laid out scenarios including weaker investment returns, falling valuations and rising unemployment, stressing they were scenarios, not forecasts.
headlines.why_it_matters: A fully priced hike keeps upward pressure on the 10Y (5.15%) and on growth multiples — the rate backdrop behind Monday's tech slide, not a separate story.

headlines.headline: Amazon plans to invest $7B in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, on top of $4B already contracted. Shares were -0.65% premarket, after falling 3.34% Monday to $257.75. Carried: Amazon lost 40 Leo satellites in Sunday's ULA Vulcan failure; the next Leo launch is an Ariane 6 flight Nov 23.
headlines.why_it_matters: Long-term infrastructure spend, not a near-term earnings driver — the premarket dip is the broad tech tape, not the announcement.

headlines.headline: Megacap board: all seven fell Monday — AAPL -0.98% to $352.78, MSFT -1.12% to $517.99, META -2.38% to $626.41, TSLA -2.69% to $379.74, AMZN -3.34%, GOOGL -4.07% to $283.72, NVDA -4.12%. Premarket drift continues: META -0.87% at $620.95 (5:00 AM ET) and MSFT -1.51% in European trading. No fresh company headline drove the laggards — broad AI-trade de-risking into Nvidia's print.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selling is concentrated in AI-levered names rather than a broad risk-off move — positioning into tonight's print, not stock-specific problems.

headlines.headline: Red Cat (RCAT) -24.9% premarket after Q3 missed badly: EPS -$0.26 vs -$0.20 expected and revenue $11.77M vs $39.51M expected. Cerebras (CBRS) -1.43% premarket despite topping Q3 revenue estimates and raising full-year Core revenue guidance.
headlines.why_it_matters: Earnings misses are being punished hard and even beats are fading — the tape's mood into Nvidia's print is unforgiving.
